_about: FIGURES / STEPS / SEQUENCES — Patryk's movement vocabulary, leader side. This is a QUERYABLE PARTS BIN for composing dances and improvising, not an encyclopedia. Two arrays: `figures` (curated, described moves) and `sequences` (the cheap index of his repertoire — stubs, ratings, source links). The collaborator reads both and cross-links them by id.
_principles: All fields optional. A 4-tag stub is a complete-enough entry. Never interrogate for every field.
Schema GROWS FROM USE: when a one-off note gains a real query use-case, promote it to a field (this is how `trajectory` and `spotlight` were born).
The high-value axes for querying: trajectory, spotlight, dance_qualities, gears, floor_safety, usage, musical_fit, rating.
GDrive is the master for sequences; store links, never duplicate the source.
_id_convention: fig-<slug> / seq-<NNN>. Reference qualities by qual-<slug>, musicality ideas by mus-<slug>, concepts/plans by con-<slug>.

_field_notes.trajectory: list of: linear (progressive/travels) | circular (orbits a point) | lateral (side travel) | in_place (no travel)
_field_notes.spotlight: leader | follower | both  — who is carrying more of the movement/work / who the eye is on. 'both' is earned, not a default.
_field_notes.usage: social | spectacular | show  — the intent/context the move belongs to
_field_notes.dance_qualities: list of qual-<slug> ids and/or free words
_field_notes.gears: list of embrace gears (con-embrace-states) the figure works well in: viento | rayo | agua | tierra | fuego. Promoted 2026-07-02 after the first milonga field test showed figures are GEAR-LOCKED — a gear is a vocabulary filter, not just a quality preset. Absent = not yet assessed on the floor. Rule: a figure the current gear can't serve waits for the next section seam.
_field_notes.rating: Patryk's own 0-10 preference for the move (NOT progress tracking — a 'how much I like/trust this' signal he filters by)

figures.name: Caminata (forward walk)
figures.short_description: The forward walking step — the most versatile basic; a carrier for rhythm, melody, and syncopation.
figures.detailed_description: A single forward step. Progressive by default (you travel forward); add a turn/pivot and the same walk becomes circular. Its value is range: the same step can be slowed almost to a pause, stretched melodically, driven on the beat, or syncopated — without becoming a different figure. The timing of the weight transfer is the expressive knob.
figures.musical_fit: Almost anything — marcato rhythm, legato melodic lines, syncopation. Advances the line of dance, so it's also the default ronda-safe move.
figures.notes: Works in EVERY gear — each gear re-voices the same walk. A CARRIER figure — range of quality AND range of trajectory, not a fixed shape. The proof-of-concept for the whole anti-monotony idea: vary the quality, not the figure.

figures.name: Caminata outside (outside-partner walk)
figures.short_description: Forward walk on the outside track — stepping outside the partner's line (outside-partner position) rather than straight into her.
figures.notes: Walk variant; gears from the floor notes (F/T/A). A caminata that changes TRACK rather than shape — the outside position is the door into cross system and outside-partner sacadas.

figures.name: Caminata in cross system (sistema cruzado)
figures.short_description: Walking in cross system — leader and follower on opposite feet — instead of parallel system. A system change, not a new shape.
figures.notes: Walk variant; gears from the floor notes (F/A). Cross system is the setup for sacadas and many giro entries; reached cleanly from the outside walk. Cf. seq-097 (changing systems), seq-051 (man's crossing).

figures.name: Caminata doble tiempo (double-time walk)
figures.short_description: The walk taken in double time — two steps inside one beat's stride; a rhythmic acceleration of the caminata, not a new shape.
figures.notes: Walk variant; gear from the floor notes: RAYO only. Telling result — doubling the walk narrows it to the one gear that can voice fast/sharp/contained. The single-gear tag IS the insight.

figures.name: Caminata with turns (chain)
figures.short_description: A travelling walk threaded with turns/chain (cadena) — the walk keeps progressing down the floor while the turns add spice. Net-linear, locally circular.
figures.notes: Walk variant; gears from the floor notes (F/A). A clean live example of the progression-vs-shape split we mapped: NET-progresses (so it files as linear) but carries circular content. Cf. seq-074 'Caminata girada'.

figures.name: Caminata with twists
figures.short_description: A travelling walk laced with body twists (dissociation / contra-body) — the walk progresses while the torso twists add texture. Net-linear.
figures.notes: Walk variant; gears from the floor notes (F/R) — both members of the STRONG family (Fuego wide, Rayo contained). Reads as: the twist wants the engaged/strong frame to stay clean, not the soft gears. Cf. seq-079 'Effective twists'.

figures.name: Back ocho (ocho atrás)
figures.short_description: Follower's backward figure-eight; led from dissociation, not the arms. Rhythmic, not melodic.
figures.detailed_description: Two techniques. HIP-FIRST: rotate the hip → project the leg → transfer → close (big, dynamic, open embrace; also the back-sacada mechanic). LEG-FIRST: a relaxed leg circles back and the swing turns the hip (small, intimate, close embrace; 'catch her foot' for gancho/pasada).
figures.leader_action: Dissociate (torsion low, just above the hip); mark the pivot with the chest, stay off the arms. On the step turn the foot outside to support the next pivot; stay low.
figures.musical_fit: Rhythmic music; voice the beat. Can progress down the floor (unlike the front ocho).
figures.notes: Rhythmic, not melodic (per Patryk — overrides the legato tag from the original mined notes). GEAR MAPPING follows the two techniques: hip-first = Agua (the hip/spiral engine — same mechanic as the back sacada), leg-first = Tierra (small, close, catch-her-foot); Viento carries the neutral social ocho.

figures.name: Front ocho (ocho adelante)
figures.short_description: Follower's forward figure-eight; rhythmic, side-to-side or circular. No linear progression.
figures.notes: Trajectory asymmetry worth remembering: back ocho can go linear, front ocho can't — only lateral/circular.

figures.name: Ochito (small ocho)
figures.short_description: Smaller, faster ochos — quick and compact. The go-to tool for a run of quicks.
figures.detailed_description: = ochos dialed down in size and up in speed; rhythmic, good for quick passages and the 'q×6' burst in a playful phrase.
figures.notes: Kept standalone deliberately — it's a distinctive tool Patryk reaches for by name, even though it's derivable from ocho + {small, fast}.

figures.name: Calesita (carousel)
figures.short_description: Leader orbits the follower while she stays on her axis — a carousel. Spotlight on her. Mostly legato, delicate.
figures.detailed_description: Follower suspended on one axis; leader walks a circle around her, she can decorate. Mainly a legato, delicate feeling; can be taken staccato.
figures.musical_fit: Slow, romantic, melodic passages; feature the follower.
figures.notes: Parks on one spot — doesn't advance the ronda, mind the lane behind you. The INVERSE of the giro (leader orbits follower vs follower orbits leader). 'Sometimes staccato' is the exception; legato is home.

figures.name: Ocho cortado (cut ocho)
figures.short_description: The follower's ocho is interrupted and rocked back to a cross — a compact, rhythmic close-embrace staple.
figures.detailed_description: A 'cut' ocho: lead out, check/rock (rebote), bring her back across to the cross. Sits on a 1-and-2, 3-and-4 syncopation — a rhythm tool more than a travel tool.
figures.musical_fit: Rhythmic, driving music (D'Arienzo feel). Lands the 1&2, 3&4 quick cell. Stays on its spot — a crowded-floor workhorse.
figures.notes: Spotlight left unset — wasn't obvious, Patryk hasn't said. Tierra lists it by name (quiet-but-rhythmic close embrace); Rayo serves the loud/sharp version of the same cell.

figures.name: The cross (cruzada)
figures.short_description: Follower crosses one foot in front of the other; a hub with many exits. Collects her onto one axis.
figures.detailed_description: Leading the cross as a real lead (through the body and the track of the walk) rather than relying on her habit. Because it collects her feet onto a single axis, it's a clean entry to the calesita.
figures.notes: Works in every gear — a neutral collection all embraces share, which also makes it the natural SEAM for a gear shift (she's on one axis, the frame is free to reconfigure). A hub with many ENTRIES as well as exits — reachable from unexpected approaches (e.g. a circular step right around the leader into a back cross, seen in La Clavada Section 3). The linear→circular HINGE: it collects her onto one axis, the clean release into a giro or calesita.

figures.name: Giro (turn)
figures.short_description: Follower travels a front-side-back grapevine around the leader, who stays on his axis as the still centre.
figures.notes: The INVERSE of the calesita (follower orbits leader vs leader orbits follower). A circular caminata at a different scale. USAGE NOTE (from La Clavada): can be the ENGINE of forward travel — a circular figure that still progresses the line of dance, not only an on-the-spot turn.

figures.name: Boleo
figures.short_description: A whip of the follower's relaxed lower leg, a REACTION to a reversal of the hip/dissociation — never a kick.
figures.detailed_description: The knee-pendulum rebound: from a back-ocho/dissociation, the energy reverses and the relaxed lower leg whips. Front and back, linear and circular. Relaxed = fast. Lead from energy/dissociation, never yank the arm.
figures.musical_fit: Climaxes, accents, the end of a dramatic phrase. Punctuation, not a sentence.
figures.notes: High floorcraft cost — open floor or practica ONLY, never a crowded milonga. Wants the load/release frame: Fuego for the big version, Rayo for the contained/social-scale whip (per con-load-legato-spend-accent).

figures.name: Gancho (hook)
figures.short_description: A hooking flick of the leg between the partner's legs — a REACTION to a sharp reversal of direction/dissociation; the relaxed lower leg whips around and hooks. Cousin of the boleo (boleo whips OUT, gancho hooks IN).
figures.leader_action: Lead the sharp reversal from the body/dissociation; create the leg to hook into; never pull it with the arm.
figures.musical_fit: Sharp accents — voices the quick 'pam-pam' hits at the end of a sustained note.
figures.notes: From the show (La Clavada Section 2), their main accent tool. Wants the Abrazo del Fuego gear (load + release); the compact close-embrace social gancho maps to Rayo (small + sharp + stopping power). A compact close-embrace social gancho exists, but the big version is needs_space. Promoted from sequence-only (seq-022/024/028/030/037) to a real figure.
source_links: La Clavada — Brenno Marques & Fátima Caracoche, MSTF 2025 Poreč (video obs)

figures.name: Sacada (displacement)
figures.short_description: Stepping into the space the partner's leg is leaving, displacing their free leg — a displacement figure. The back sacada gets its quality from the hips.
figures.musical_fit: Displacement accents; 'little sacadas' punctuating a rhythmic line.
figures.notes: From the show (La Clavada Section 2) as 'little sacadas' — displacement accents. The BACK SACADA quality comes from the hips → wants the Abrazo del Agua gear; sacadas AT SCALE are Fuego's list. Promoted from sequence-only (seq-021/023/026).
source_links: La Clavada — Brenno Marques & Fátima Caracoche, MSTF 2025 Poreč (video obs)

figures.name: Parada (stop)
figures.short_description: Leader stops/blocks the follower's foot with his — a punctuation that often resolves a small rhythmic run. The pause-as-move; pairs with barrida and pasada.
figures.musical_fit: A stop / the end of a phrase; quiet rhythmic sections; a held beat she can decorate over.
figures.notes: Closed Section 3 of La Clavada (the quiet rhythmic part). A resolution/punctuation for small on-the-spot vocabulary; pairs with the barrida (seq-034) and pasada. New figure — wasn't in the graph at all.
source_links: La Clavada — Brenno Marques & Fátima Caracoche, MSTF 2025 Poreč (video obs)

figures.name: Tap (tapped step / golpecito)
figures.short_description: A leader-side decoration: the forward foot taps/touches the floor as an active articulation before (or instead of) a full weight change. A small rhythmic embellishment.
figures.musical_fit: Rhythmic accents; quiet-but-rhythmic sections; voicing a quick without travelling.
figures.notes: Seen as the leader's forward-leg tap in La Clavada Section 3 ('looks nice'). Filed as a FIGURE/decoration, not a quality — it's a discrete action, not a how-danced adjective (guarding the qualities line).
source_links: La Clavada — Brenno Marques & Fátima Caracoche, MSTF 2025 Poreč (video obs)

_sequences_about: Patryk's repertoire from the 'Step of the day' series (his GDrive list is master). CHEAP INDEX only: genre + orchestra-character + his rating + usage + source. No internal steps unless we work one in detail (then it graduates to the `figures` array). `rating` is his own 0-10. character is inferred from the orchestra; usage is a best-guess from the title — both editable. TRAJECTORY + GEARS (added 2026-08-10): a sequence may carry `trajectory` and `gears` once field-assessed. Rule (Patryk): a sequence's trajectory is its NET path down the floor — it can be `linear` even when its component figures (gancho / sacada / barrida) are not. Absent = not yet assessed.
